query: For refractory materials, experiments at the solid-to-fluid transition are difficult and yield sparse, scattered data, while the large compositional space of high-entropy systems makes systematic screening impractical. DFT free-energy studies can determine the transition from the crossing of solid and dense-fluid Gibbs energies and provide associated thermodynamic properties, but their reliance on extensive ab initio molecular dynamics makes them costly. TOR-TILD has shown high efficiency for elemental and binary systems, yet becomes substantially slower for multicomponent systems. Any broadly useful approach must retain ab initio-level accuracy, represent all thermodynamic effects identified as important, treat both phases around the transition, and remain practical across relevant compositions and temperatures. For a multicomponent high-entropy material in these high-temperature states, what single intervention could improve determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and causal mechanism, its predicted outcome relative to existing experimental and computational baselines, its boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive experiment or benchmark that would falsify it.

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How to screen for single-phase high-entropy alloys using an in-house thermodynamic database and binary priority lists?. System: Co,Fe,Mn,Ni,Zn-containing high-entropy alloys (quaternary, quinary, and senary systems). Processing: Mechanical alloying of elemental powders (Co >99.0%, Fe >99.99%, Mn >99.9%, Ni >99.9%, Zn >99.9%) in a planetary ball mill at 300 rpm for 30 h with 5 mm stainless balls, ball-to-powder weight ratio of 10:1, and toluene as process control agent; followed by compaction, sealing in a vacuum quartz tube, and heating at 900 °C for 24 h with a heating rate of 50 °C/min, then air cooling.. Test conditions: Phase identification performed using an X-ray diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation on milled powders and heat-treated samples.. Own digest: Paper card. Question: Which equimolar quinary combinations of 40 metallic elements form thermodynamically stable single-phase solid solutions, and what are the driving factors (mixing enthalpy, melting point, intermetallic competition) governing their formation?. System: Equimolar quinary alloys from 40 elements (e.g., AlCoMnNiV, CoFeMnNiZn, Cantor alloy CoCrFeMnNi). Processing: High-throughput density-functional theory (DFT) calculations using a binary regular solid-solution model; experimental synthesis via arc-melting (AlCoMnNiV) and mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering (CoFeMnNiZn). Test conditions: Thermodynamic stability assessed at temperatures ranging from 800 to 1600 K, with optimal screening at T = 0.9Tm; experimental validation via SEM, XRD, and EDS after heat treatment at 1373 K (AlCoMnNiV) and 1073–1273 K (CoFeMnNiZn).
